what_it_does: Modern chips pack billions of transistors into incredibly small areas, making it nearly impossible to debug or diagnose failures without special tools. This paper presents a tiny probe—a microscopic sensor that can monitor electrical signals inside the chip without disrupting them. Traditional test equipment at the board level adds unwanted electrical loading (capacitance and inductance) that distorts signals, especially at tiny feature sizes. The innovation is a high-impedance probe design—one that draws very little current—integrated with a sensitive amplifier on the same chip, allowing accurate signal monitoring from DC (direct current) all the way up to 50 gigahertz (radio frequencies), all without damaging the signal.
